A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IP/IP Ensemble research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic-data, noisy-label, NLP fairness, and adversarial-defense experiments, with additional analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments in Sections 4–7 and Appendix A and reports additional NLP comparator results.

M1.justification: The converged-model gradient inner product, fairness and robustness extensions, and dropout-based ensemble remain unchanged. Rewriting Equations (2)–(4) and moving the ensemble formulas from Appendix B to Section 5 do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic datasets, CIFAR-10N variants, CIFAR-100N, Animal-10N, RTE, CoLA, QNLI, Bank, CelebA, and JigsawToxicity. The ViT and MLP-Mixer evaluations were already present in v2’s appendix.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 3 adds TDA and GEX to the reported NLP comparison relative to v2 Figure 5. TDA’s addition to the speed chart redisplays a comparator whose timing was already reported in v2 Table 7; other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Section 4 reports 200 half-moon training samples, but Appendix B.1.1 reports 250. v3 Section 4 consistently specifies 200, correcting the reported setting without establishing that experiments were rerun. The retained benchmarks’ splits, metrics, architectures, and training budgets otherwise remain stable.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 3 and its accompanying diagnostic of validation and detrimental-sample gradient directions are removed. The synthetic fairness/robustness analysis and removal-rate, dropout, ensemble-size, and architecture analyses remain, moving from Appendix C to Appendix A.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5 explicitly describes five independent identify-and-retrain runs and states that both the ResNet and ViT/MLP-Mixer tables average five runs. v2 explicitly documents five ResNet retrainings but does not similarly specify the architecture table’s run count. This expands reporting rather than demonstrating more runs.

E6.justification: The NLP plot revises TracIn’s RTE and QNLI points and adds TDA/GEX results. The synthetic gradient-angle findings of 0.66° and 94.36° disappear with v2 Figure 3. Corresponding accuracy, defense, ablation, and runtime tables retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3 and Appendix A’s region-by-region order-consistency argument, including the assumption α < 45° and Table 3, are removed without a replacement proof. The underlying influence, IP, fairness, robustness, and ensemble formulas remain equivalent; v3 instead supplies qualitative gradient-alignment and Hessian-regularization reasoning.

C1.justification: v3 withdraws the conclusion’s claim of proving order-consistency and explicitly emphasizes studying an existing Hessian-free method. The principal claims about utility, fairness, robustness, and dropout-ensemble enhancement remain.

C2.justification: The central explanation shifts from geometric order-consistency to gradient alignment and the difficulties of regularizing Hessian inverses. Section 3 adds a substantive failure discussion for under-trained models and unstable gradients. Conversely, v2 Appendix D’s limitations concerning heterogeneous data, broader applicability, and computational barriers to ImageNet-scale evaluation are removed.

D1.justification: v3 replaces v2 Appendix E’s code-upon-request statement with an anonymous repository link and specifies that NLP utility/fairness scores form one joint ranking before pruning. Most dataset, hyperparameter, and hardware details are relocated into the main text. The explicit CIFAR-100N noise rate of 40.20% is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 acknowledges Charpiat et al. as earlier final-checkpoint IP work and adds discussion of Deng et al.’s efficient ensembles and TRAK. References to Bingham–Mannila dimensionality reduction and scikit-learn are removed. These refine attribution and positioning while retaining most related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method rationale, and synthetic-experiment narrative receive substantial rewriting. Dataset and training descriptions from v2 Appendix B are integrated into Sections 4–7, the appendices are consolidated, and new failure-condition and experimental-roadmap passages alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 Figures 1, 3, and 7 and the order-consistency table are removed. The speed and NLP plots are redrawn, including an expanded CoLA accuracy axis and revised legends; robustness boxes are reordered. Figures and appendix tables are extensively repositioned, while the retained synthetic plots preserve their content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through clearer prior-work attribution, more complete NLP comparisons, explicit failure conditions, and concrete code-access instructions. Withdrawing the proof claim also makes the framing more cautious. These gains are limited by removal of broader applicability and resource limitations and unexplained revisions to TracIn’s plotted results; the method and most empirical evidence remain unchanged.
